heldout_proposal.note: PROPOSAL for the user's approval — edit this file (and the per-case 'split' fields above) to change it. Held-out cases were chosen to span different (metric, app, window) combinations plus hard cases held back entirely: a country breakdown (b10), an app breakdown (b15), a segment filter (b19), a registry lookup (b23), a per-viewer metric (b30), a WhatsApp series (b36), a vague WhatsApp weather question (b37), the app-scoped stickiness variant (b39), the WhatsApp diagnosis-priority conversation (c2), and the ranking follow-up (c8). HONEST LIMITATION: these 10 cases were already used while developing the planner (they are part of the existing 49-case benchmark that drove fixes), so this held-out set is 'held out from future fixes', not pristine. Truly fresh held-out cases — new (metric, app, window) combinations never run against the planner — arrive with slice 2's ~101 new cases. The 120/30 target split in the design draft applies at 150 cases; at 49 cases the proposal is 39 dev / 10 held-out.
heldout_proposal.rationale: Different (metric, app, window) combinations plus hard cases held back entirely.

rules: The harness runs dev-only, held-out-only, or all — never a mixed aggregate. Held-out results are reported in a separate table; they must never be folded into the dev aggregate or used to decide a fix.

A fix decided against a dev failure is re-verified on held-out only by reporting, never by tuning against held-out failures. If a held-out failure drives a change, that case moves to dev in the next benchmark version and the version number changes.

The manifest version (v1) and the eval files must agree: the harness refuses to run if a case id is missing from, or duplicated in, either side, or if the data pin (users, counts, max date) does not match the data dir.
New cases (slice 2) get a manifest entry with family + split at creation time, before any fix is made against them. The version bumps to v2 when the case set changes.
